title: Unveiling chemical composition of peppermint oil and its bioactivities compared with (R)‐(+)‐limonene: antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and insecticidal perspectives
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Peppermint (Mentha piperita L.) essential oil (MPEO) is recognized for its broad-spectrum antimicrobial properties and potential applications in food preservation. This study aimed to determine whether the bioactivity of MPEO is attributable to (R)-(+)-limonene or whether the complete essential oil provides higher efficacy due to interactions among multiple constituents.

RESULTS

MPEO was characterized using GC–MS and evaluated for antimicrobial activity in vitro against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and yeasts, and in situ in the vapor phase on strawberries, plums, beetroot, and tomatoes. Antibiofilm activity against Salmonella enterica was assessed using crystal violet assay and MALDI-TOF MS, while insecticidal activity was tested against Callosobruchus maculatus and Megabruchidius dorsalis. GC–MS revealed a menthol chemotype dominated by menthol (54.2%), with isomenthone (8.4%), isomenthol acetate (5.7%), 1,8-cineole (5.7%), linalool (3.1%), β-caryophyllene (3.5%), limonene (2.7%), and α-pinene (1.5%). MPEO generally produced larger inhibition zones and lower minimum inhibitory concentration values than (R)-(+)-limonene, and stronger in situ growth suppression. Antibiofilm activity was demonstrated in both assays. In insecticidal tests, limonene was more effective than MPEO at 6.25–50%, while both treatments were nearly fully effective at 100%.

CONCLUSION

MPEO showed greater overall antimicrobial efficacy than (R)-(+)-limonene, supporting the importance of interactions among its constituents. Its combined antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and insecticidal activities indicate potential for use as a natural bio-preservative and in integrated pest management. © 2026 The Author(s).
